item.title: Absolute Discounting
item.description: Absolute discounting is a smoothing technique for n-gram models.

item.title: Activation Function
item.description: An activation function is a tool used in neural networks to introduce non-linearity to the outputs of artificial neurons in the network.

item.title: Ad Hoc Hypothesis
item.description: An ad hoc hypothesis is an additional explanatory factor which is added to a theory to protect that theory from potentially falsifying evidence.

item.title: Adaptive Algorithms
item.description: An adaptive algorithm is an algorithm whose behaviour is dynamically altered during the course of its run time based on new information provided after each iteration.

item.title: Adjacency Matrix
item.description: An adjacency matrix is a square matrix which is used to represent the all possible connections in a given graph.

item.title: Algorithms
item.description: An algorithm is a procedure consisting of well-defined steps, taking some set of inputs to produce some set of outputs.

item.title: Antonymy
item.description: Antonymy describes a relationship between words which have opposite meanings.

item.title: Arithmetic Mean
item.description: The arithmetic mean is a measure of central tendency, defined as the sum of a set of values, divided by the number of values in the set.

item.title: Artificial Neuron
item.description: An artificial neuron is a component of a neural network which comprises of a mathematical function, taking inputs from, and producing outputs for, other artificial neurons in the network.

item.title: Assortativity
item.description: Assortativity refers to the tendency for vertices in a graph to connect to other similar vertices.
